findings.message: New private DB helper `GetPropertyDefinitionIdsFromDbAsync` re-implements a query that already exists, word-for-word, on `ResourcesTestClient`. `ResourcesTestClient.GetResourcePropertyDefinitionsFromDbAsync(Guid resourceTypeId)` (ResourcesTestClient.cs:203-211) already does `db.ResourcePropertyDefinitions.IgnoreQueryFilters().Where(x => x.ResourceTypeId == resourceTypeId).ToListAsync()` — the new method is the same DbSet, same filter, same predicate, only projecting `.Select(d => d.Id)` afterward. integration-test-infrastructure.md establishes TestClient as the single place for DB methods precisely so a query only exists once ("TestClient centralises route strings and request shapes in one place... a route change requires updating only the TestClient, not every test method that calls it"; "IgnoreQueryFilters() is mandatory on all DB methods in TestClient"). This diff instead puts a second, private copy of the same query in the test class.
findings.evidence: SoftDeleteResourceTypeReadPathTests.cs:144-153: `private async Task<List<Guid>> GetPropertyDefinitionIdsFromDbAsync(Guid resourceTypeId) { ... return await db.ResourcePropertyDefinitions.IgnoreQueryFilters().Where(d => d.ResourceTypeId == resourceTypeId).Select(d => d.Id).ToListAsync(); }` vs. the pre-existing ResourcesTestClient.cs:203-211 `internal async Task<List<ResourcePropertyDefinition>> GetResourcePropertyDefinitionsFromDbAsync(Guid resourceTypeId) => db.ResourcePropertyDefinitions.IgnoreQueryFilters().Where(x => x.ResourceTypeId == resourceTypeId).ToListAsync();`
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the private helper; call `client.GetResourcePropertyDefinitionsFromDbAsync(resourceType.Id)` and project `.Select(d => d.Id)` at the two call sites (line 116-117).

rule_candidate.description: Detect near-duplicate DB query methods (same DbSet + same Where predicate shape) added by a diff across a TestClient file and any other file in the same IntegrationTests project — near-duplicate detector for EF LINQ query bodies.

findings.message: `CreatePropertyDefinitionInDbAsync` and `CreatePropertyValueInDbAsync` are full entity-factory methods (call `{Entity}.Create(...)`, open a DI scope, `Add` + `SaveChangesAsync`) — exactly the "Standard entity factory" shape the convention defines — but they are private methods on the test class instead of living in a dedicated `Clients/{Entity}Factory.cs`. The convention states infrastructure is split into three components created "once per module and extended as the module grows", with factories explicitly filed at `Clients/{Entity}Factory.cs`, so other tests needing a property definition/value precondition cannot reuse this logic and a second ad-hoc copy is likely next time.
findings.evidence: SoftDeleteResourceTypeReadPathTests.cs:120-142: `private async Task<ResourcePropertyDefinition> CreatePropertyDefinitionInDbAsync(...) { var definition = ResourcePropertyDefinition.Create(...); ... db.ResourcePropertyDefinitions.Add(definition); await db.SaveChangesAsync(); return definition; }` and the sibling `CreatePropertyValueInDbAsync` — compare to the file-path rule at integration-test-infrastructure.md "2. Factories — Clients/{Entity}Factory.cs".
findings.suggested_fix: Extract both methods into `Clients/ResourcesPropertyDefinitionFactory.cs` and `Clients/ResourcesPropertyValueFactory.cs` (or one combined factory), following the existing `ResourcesResourceTypeFactory` / `ResourcesResourceInstanceFactory` pattern, and inject them via the test constructor like the other factories in this file.

rule_candidate.description: Flag any class under an IntegrationTests project, outside `Clients/`, that calls `GetRequiredService<{Module}DbContext>()` to `Add(...)` an entity — Arrange-phase entity creation must go through a `Clients/{Entity}Factory` class.
